notes: The mirror image of Lure of the Wildcat and the reason a group must never be assumed from a list: bullet 2 says 'Speak to the following NPCs in Western Adoulin in order', so the seven are seven ORDERED steps and not an unordered set. A group here would draw all seven at once and mislead the player, since this quest is a patrol ROUTE and following it 'to the letter' is the whole premise. All seven are in one zone, so the marker walks the route with you. The sub-sub-bullets are the line each NPC repeats once you have exhausted their dialogue -- a stop condition, not a separate action -- so they stay in the note. The Western Adoulin patrol route key item resolves (2274) and is the only observable in the quest; the page calls it Temporary, which here means it is taken back at the end, not that it is invisible. Adoulin is not one of the nine fame regions, so the fame gate is raw-only.

notes: Six bullets, four steps. Bullet 2 is a Note, not an action -- it is the 18:00-06:00 window advice attached to the customs check, and game time is not observable, so it is a flag and a note rather than a step. Bullet 3 ('Travel to Port Jeuno') is merged into bullet 4 rather than kept as its own travel rung: its destination zone is the same zone bullet 4's NPC stands in, so a separate travel step would be a duplicate marker on the same place, and everything under bullet 3 is routing advice (Home Point warp is fine, no San d'Orian ticket needed). The real content of bullet 3 is its warning -- you must still clear the Air Travel Agency or the package is damaged -- which is bullet 4's step. 'Quest Reqs: Tenshodo Membership' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate; Previous is empty, so prev stays empty and the membership is flagged. The Airship Pass is a held key item rather than a gate, so it rides on the customs step where it is actually risked -- being caught revokes it and fails the quest. The After-the-walkthrough Notes are fame trivia and patch history, not steps. Header spells the giver Portaure in Start and in bullets 1 and 6; the Notes section's 'Portuare' is a typo and is ignored.

notes: An escort, which is the worst shape for a ladder: bullets 4 to 8 are one moving fight that walks from a bridge to the sea to a lake in the north, and the page never says which of the seven monsters he fishes up appears at which stop. So they are ONE step carrying all seven, with bullet 11's roster as the source -- inventing a per-stop split would be exactly the guessing this rebuild avoids, and 'at least one' plus 'three more' is a count nothing reports. Bullet 9 is split off because it is the only observable moment in the escort: killing The Big One is what grants Travonce's escort award. Bullet 3 is written as a warning ('do not talk to Travonce until all party members are in the area') but a player reads it as the instruction to talk to Travonce in Lufaise Meadows to start the escort, so it is kept as a step with the caveat in its note. Its sub-bullets -- level cap 45, no Trust, outside help cannot cast on capped players or on the fished-up monsters -- are conditions, not steps. The 13:00-16:00 window on bullet 2 is game time and unobservable, which is the main reason for the medium. The header's 'Item Reqs: [KI] Travonce's escort award' is not a precondition at all -- you earn it in bullet 9 and hold it for the hand-in -- so it is recorded where it is actually used. 'The Big One' is taken as the monster's own name because the page capitalises it as one; if the live mob is named otherwise that step simply loses its marker. STAGE D: gates.level nulled. The header's 'Level: 45' is the escort's level CAP restated -- bullet 3's own sub-bullet says 'The level cap for this quest is 45' -- not a minimum you must reach to accept it, and the runtime turns gates.level into a hard 'level 45 required, you are N' prereq. Emitting it would declare an escort whose whole point is capping you at 45 out of reach for everyone under 45. Nothing else on this quest is altered: bullet 3 stays a step because talking to Travonce out in Lufaise Meadows is what starts the escort, the seven fished-up monsters stay on one rung because the page never says which appears where, and Travonce's escort award is earned at bullet 9 and so is step 5's evidence, not a reward.

notes: Monk artifact quest, so 'Level: 50+ Monk' is BOTH gates -- level 50 and jobs MNK -- and 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field, which means false. Both entries under Item Reqs are key items the walkthrough itself hands you (bullets 2 and 4), not things you bring, so they are recorded as evidence where they are earned. Bullet 2 is one journey, not two: Qu'Bia Arena is entered from Fei'Yin, so a separate Fei'Yin rung would be a marker on somewhere you only pass through; the cutscene actually fires as you zone back OUT, which is in the note. Bullet 4 is genuinely three actions and is split into three -- click the Hide Flap, kill the two NMs it pops, then find the flap again and check it -- because the middle one is a fight and the last one is the only place the scroll can come from. The Hide Flap MOVES to a random hut after any player searches, so its (F-7) is a hint and not a fixed point; the page itself gives (F-7)/(G-7) as a pair, which is the grid conflict. Deloknok is the Paladin and Bilopdop the Monk. The multi-player and cooldown sub-bullets under bullet 4 are conditions, not steps.

notes: The whole walkthrough is one wikitable blob with no top-level numbering, so every step cites bullet 1 -- there is only one rendered block to cite. Reading it as a player: talk to the fortune teller, farm a lens, soak the lens, collect what it becomes, bring that back. The 'Crystal Ball' he asks for is flavour -- no such item resolves, and what you actually make and hand over is the Divination Sphere -- so it is named only in a note and never used as a target or an item. The Ahriman Lens is Ex and drops from Evil Eye monsters in three different zones, and a step has one zone, so the obtain step is deliberately zone-less with the three named in its note. 'Evil Eye' is recorded as the mob because the page names it; it is a family as much as an individual, hence the flag. The one-minute Earth-time wait between trading the lens and checking the Rockwell is folded into the examine step's note rather than made a wait rung -- nothing reports a timer, and steps 3 and 4 are the same object and therefore one marker anyway. The long Voidwatch/Hyacinth-stratum/cruor material is advice on how to reach Attohwa Chasm quickly and is not part of the quest.

notes: The header names 'Nashu, Marjami Ravine' as the giver, but Nashu does not appear anywhere in the walkthrough. What the walkthrough actually does is talk to Zaffeld in Eastern Adoulin (J-8) first and return to Zaffeld last -- he is the bookend NPC -- while the quest only enters your log on the zone-in cutscene in Marjami Ravine, which is presumably where Nashu is. So start is moved to Zaffeld, which is a marker MOVE rather than a removal, and the header string is kept verbatim in raw. Bullet 3 is pure routing inside Marjami Ravine -- Frontier Station to Bivouac #2, southeast, tunnel by the watch tower at (J-9/10), on to (I-10), up the vine at the tent -- and merges into bullet 4's examine rather than becoming a travel rung inside the zone it is already in. The Seat of Gramk-Droog is examined three times with a fight in the middle, and each examine is a real distinct action the page separates, so all three are kept even though they share one marker. Bullet 7's target is written only as 'the Hospital' at (I-9) across from Flapano; Flapano is the landmark, not the target, and the Hospital keeps the step's confidence at medium because the page never gives it a fuller name. Nothing in this quest is observable -- there is no key item anywhere in it -- so the ladder runs on the session latch throughout. The Notes section is translation trivia and a Bayld buy-back for the earring; neither is a step. STAGE D: quest confidence lowered high -> medium. The eight rungs do match the eight bullets and the zone crossings are right, but two load-bearing fields are inferred rather than read: the start is recovered from bullet 1 because the header's giver Nashu appears nowhere in the walkthrough, and step 7's target is the bare common noun 'the Hospital' with no fuller name on the page. A header and a walkthrough that disagree about who gives the quest is the medium case by the guide's own definition. The ladder itself is left exactly as drafted.

notes: Twenty recruits in a wikitable, and the whole point of this quest is that they may be visited in any order -- bullet 3 only asks that all twenty have been spoken to. A strict ladder would mark Deidogg and then nothing else until you happened to walk past him, so all twenty share one group and draw at once. They span four zones, so each keeps its own zone and grid: one step, one zone. Metalworks (G-8) legitimately holds two of them, Invincible Shield and Raibaht. The Blue Sentinel badge is a key item (744) and is the quest's only observable, granted at step 1 and surrendered at the end, so it is step 1's evidence and step 22's held item. The Blue invitation card is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done and is never used as evidence. The After-the-walkthrough Notes are about what to do with the card afterwards -- Naja Salaheem's Imperial currency and Alib-Mufalib's 300 gil teleport -- and belong to other quests, not this ladder.
